why: Shane asked to see what a fully populated site looks like before the pre-pilot cleanup gate is run. These are DEMONSTRATION pools, not real D2 jobs.
readThisFirst: These use REALISTIC job numbers (D2-10xx) on purpose, so the views, timeline lanes, launchpad and summary emails show what a real multi-pool site looks like. A TEST- prefix would have appeared in every assignment title and defeated the exercise.

The cost of that choice: flows/testdata/cleanup.js will NOT auto-delete them. Its classifier only removes rows it can prove are ours (a TEST- job number, or the D2-1001 demo job) and reports everything else rather than deleting it. That caution is deliberate and correct, because after go-live those lists hold a PM's real request history.
So this manifest is the removal record. Delete these by explicit job number, via a Delete Pool Request per pool (Title must equal ConfirmJobNumber exactly), or by direct REST using the ids below.
If these are still present when the pre-pilot gate runs, cleanup.js will list them in its review table as rows held for a human decision. That is the intended behaviour, not a failure.

expectedShape.arriveAs: Status = Planned, so they dispatch nothing and raise no conflict alerts until committed to Active
expectedShape.note: All 46 template durations are still 2-day placeholders, so each pool spans roughly four and a half months regardless of real size.

alsoATest: These three were raised at the same moment, so they generate CONCURRENTLY. Nothing had previously measured concurrent pool generation. A single pool takes 7 to 17 minutes with multi-minute stalls mid-run while the flow stays healthy, so three at once may be considerably slower or may surface throttling. A stalled row count is not evidence of failure; the reliable signals are the run's action list and the request row's Status and Result.
